items.prompt: Where would 55 be inserted into this binary search tree?
hints: Start at the root and compare 55 with each node on the way down.
Go left if the key is smaller and right if it is larger, until there is no child to follow.
55 > 40 → right to 60. 55 < 60 → left to 50. 55 > 50 → it becomes the right child of 50.

options.feedback: 60 already has a left child, 50. Keep comparing until you reach an empty spot.
55 < 60, so the search goes left at 60 and never reaches 70.
55 > 40, so the search goes right at the root.

items.prompt: Searching for 30, which nodes do you visit, in order?
hints: Every search starts at the root.
Compare at each node and move to one child.

options.feedback: Yes: one node per level, from the root down.
A search always starts at the root, 40.
30 < 40, so the search goes left, not right.
Searches go from the root down, not along the leaves.

items.prompt: Is this a valid binary search tree?
hints: Check each key against every ancestor, not only its parent.
Every key in the left subtree of a node must be smaller than that node.
45 is in the left subtree of 40 but 45 > 40, so the tree is not a valid BST.

options.text: No: 45 is in the left subtree of 40 but larger than 40
options.feedback: Right. The rule holds across the whole subtree, not just between parent and child.

options.text: Yes: each node is larger than its left child and smaller than its right child
options.feedback: Checking only parent and child misses 45, which is larger than its ancestor 40.

options.text: No: 10 should be the right child of 20
options.feedback: 10 < 20, so the left child is the right place for it.

items.prompt: At most, how many nodes does a search visit in a binary search tree?
hints: Each comparison moves you down one level.
A search never moves back up or sideways.
It visits at most one node per level, so at most the height of the tree.

options.text: One per level, so at most the tree's height
options.feedback: Yes. That is why short trees search fast.
That is a linear scan. A search tree lets you skip whole subtrees.
It depends on how deep the key is.
